# wiresizes.com

> Wire gauge charts, NEC table values and calculators for sizing conductors.

## Calculators

- [Wire Size Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/wire-size-calculator): Copper and aluminum conductor size for a breaker or fuse rating from 15 to 400 A, from the 60 °C column of NEC Table 310.16 (2023) limited by 240.4(D); equipment grounding conductor from Table 250.122; voltage drop at the load current over a one-way length, stepping to larger sizes until it meets the voltage-drop target you choose.
- [Voltage Drop Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/voltage-drop-calculator): Voltage drop in volts and percent, and the power lost in the conductors, for a Table 310.16 conductor size, current, one-way length and voltage, single- or three-phase, with solid-conductor DC resistance at 75 °C calculated from NIST Handbook 100 and 109.
- [Ampacity Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/ampacity-calculator): Table 310.16 (2023) ampacity for a size, material and insulation temperature column, multiplied by the ambient correction factor from Table 310.15(B)(1)(1) and the adjustment for more than three current-carrying conductors from Table 310.15(C)(1).
- [Ground Wire Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/ground-wire-calculator): Equipment grounding conductor size in copper and in aluminum or copper-clad aluminum for an overcurrent device rated 15 A to 6000 A, from NEC Table 250.122 (2023).
- [Wire Resistance Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/wire-resistance-calculator): Resistance of one conductor and of the circuit loop at a conductor temperature, from the 20 °C values of NIST Handbook 100 (copper) and Handbook 109 (aluminum EC-H19) and their temperature coefficients, and the power lost at a given current.
- [Service Entrance Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/service-entrance-calculator): Copper and aluminum conductor sizes for a 120/240 V single-phase dwelling service or main power feeder rated 100 to 400 A, from NEC Table 310.12 (2023), and the grounding electrode conductor for each from Table 250.66.
- [Low Voltage Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/low-voltage-calculator): Copper conductor size for a DC load from the circular mils its voltage-drop target needs (CM = 2 × K × I × L ÷ VD, K from NIST Handbook 100 at 20 °C or 75 °C) and from its current in the 60 °C column of NEC Table 310.16; the larger size applies.
- [Three Phase Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/three-phase-calculator): Balanced three-phase conversion between power and line current at a line-to-line voltage and power factor, I = P ÷ (√3 × V × PF).
- [Watts to Amps](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/watts-to-amps-calculator): Current from power, voltage and power factor, I = P ÷ (V × PF) single-phase and I = P ÷ (√3 × V × PF) three-phase.
- [Amps to Watts](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/amps-to-watts-calculator): Real power, apparent power and electrical horsepower (746 W) from current, voltage and power factor.
- [Volts to Amps](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/volts-to-amps-calculator): Current from power, voltage and power factor, I = P ÷ (V × PF) single-phase and I = P ÷ (√3 × V × PF) three-phase.
- [Kilowatts to Amps](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/kilowatts-to-amps-calculator): Current, apparent power and reactive power from kilowatts, voltage and power factor, single- or three-phase.
- [kVA to Amps](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/kva-to-amps-calculator): Current from apparent power and voltage, single- or three-phase.
- [BTU to Watts](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/btu-to-watts-calculator): Btu per hour to watts and tons of refrigeration and back, with 1 Btu/h = 0.2930711 W (NIST SP 811) and 1 ton = 12,000 Btu/h.
- [Ohm's Law Calculator](https://wiresizes.com/calculators/ohms-law-calculator): Voltage, current, resistance and power from any two of them, V = I × R and P = V × I.

## Charts and guides

- [AWG Wire Size Chart](https://wiresizes.com/guides/awg-wire-size-chart): AWG sizes with diameter, cross-sectional area and solid annealed copper resistance at 20 °C from NIST Handbook 100, and copper and aluminum ampacities from NEC Table 310.16 (2023).
- [NEC Table 310.16](https://wiresizes.com/guides/nec-table-310-16): All 30 rows of NEC Table 310.16 (2023), copper and aluminum in the 60, 75 and 90 °C columns, with the 16 ambient correction rows of Table 310.15(B)(1)(1) and the adjustment factors of Table 310.15(C)(1).
- [Wire Size for 200 Amp](https://wiresizes.com/guides/wire-size-for-200-amp): 2/0 AWG copper or 4/0 AWG aluminum for a 120/240 V dwelling service, from NEC Table 310.12 (2023).
- [Wire Size for 100 Amp](https://wiresizes.com/guides/wire-size-for-100-amp): 4 AWG copper or 2 AWG aluminum for a 120/240 V dwelling service, from NEC Table 310.12 (2023).
- [Wire Size for EV Charger](https://wiresizes.com/guides/wire-size-for-ev-charger): Level 1, Level 2 and DC fast charging, the 2023 NEC rule that EV charging is a continuous load (625.42), charger specifications, and copper and aluminum wire sizes for 40 A and 50 A charger circuits.
- [Electrical Power Calculations](https://wiresizes.com/guides/electrical-power-calculations): Formulas for power, current, voltage and resistance in DC, single-phase and three-phase circuits.
- [Single vs Three Phase](https://wiresizes.com/guides/single-vs-three-phase): Single-phase and three-phase voltage systems and the power formulas for each.
- [Power Factor Explained](https://wiresizes.com/guides/power-factor-explained): Real, reactive and apparent power and power factor, PF = P ÷ S.
- [NEC Code Compliance](https://wiresizes.com/guides/nec-code-compliance): NEC overcurrent protection (standard ratings from Table 240.6(A) and the 240.4(D) small-conductor limits), grounding and bonding, the voltage drop formula and GFCI locations.

## Site

- [Home](https://wiresizes.com/): Calculator and guide links; copper sizes for 15 to 40 A circuits from the 60 °C column of NEC Table 310.16 (2023); dwelling service sizes from Table 310.12; grounding electrode conductors from Table 250.66.
- [Calculators](https://wiresizes.com/calculators): List of the calculators.
- [Guides](https://wiresizes.com/guides): List of the guides.
- [About](https://wiresizes.com/about): Who writes wiresizes.com, which sources its numbers come from, how pages are checked, and the dated list of corrections.
- [Methodology](https://wiresizes.com/methodology): The sources behind the calculators, with the edition of each, the formulas used, their limits, and the topics not covered yet.
- [Contact](https://wiresizes.com/contact): Email address for corrections, questions about a page and privacy requests.
- [Privacy notice](https://wiresizes.com/privacy): What wiresizes.com collects, which services process it, the legal basis, and how to use your data protection rights.
- [Terms of use](https://wiresizes.com/terms): Who operates wiresizes.com, what its tables and calculators are for, and what they don't cover.
- [Disclaimer](https://wiresizes.com/disclaimer): The limits of the tables and calculators on wiresizes.com, and who has the final word on an installation.
